deep.reconstruction:
There is no derivation on this page, so nothing can be reconstructed. Folio 131r has only scattered, faint pen sketches. Most are written with the sheet turned about 90°.

What is visible:
(a) Upper left: a small rounded box with an illegible mark inside, and next to it an illegible small figure or glyph.
(b) A short rotated formula. It begins '1 +' and is followed by a struck-through symbol, possibly x with an exponent. There is a bar or line beside it, perhaps a fraction bar. Nearby is a scribbled glyph.
(c) Centre right: a small square split into two cells, each with a short vertical stroke, perhaps an arrow or tick. A faint duplicate sits to its left.
(d) Centre: two pairs of overlapping loops (closed curves).
(e) Next to them: a heavily inked square with an inner square or cells containing two marks.
(f) A large, roughly drawn parallelogram (rectangle in perspective).
(g) Lower left: a vertical line segment, a faint sketched curve, and two ovals each containing a single vertical stroke.
(h) Lower centre right: a square split into two cells. The marks inside could be read as dots, or as signs (+, ÷ or ±).
(i) Faint scattered numerals or letters, unreadable.

Possible interpretations (my own suggestions, not supported by any legible text):
- The cells with paired strokes or signs could be schematic pictures of charged bodies or of oriented regions.
- The overlapping loops could be simple closed curves or regions, as in Riemann's topological sketches.
- The facing page (131v/132) is about Weber-type electrodynamic potentials: εε'/r · (dr/dt)^2, a 1/c^2 velocity term, and an iterated Laplacian. That makes a physical reading of the cell diagrams slightly more plausible. But nothing on this page states or connects any formula.
